From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: RE: Can't claim supplier profile — claim code expired after SSO

Quick findings from logs:
- The claim code generation service issues a one-time token with TTL = 15 minutes (UTC). In this case the token was created at 06:48:11Z and the vendor completed the OAuth flow at ~06:49:20Z — well within TTL. However, after the OIDC handshake our code expects an "organization" claim (org_id or company_name) to be present in the ID token to bind the session to the pending claim. Google OIDC for personal accounts doesn't include that claim by default.
- When the organization claim is missing, our frontend shows the claim code briefly but the backend cannot reconcile the session and treats the token as stale; the UI surface shows "claim expired" which is confusing.
- There's also a small timezone/display bug where the client-side checks do local time comparison against UTC and will show expiry if client's clock skew exceeds 2 minutes — some vendor laptops with automatic timezone changes can trigger that.

Recommendations:
1) Short-term: Manual provisioning (Procurement Ops) and set a Coupa mapping so the vendor receives a direct Coupa invite (bypassing claim flow). I can generate a manual invite link that uses a single-use token with an explicit organization parameter.
2) Medium-term: Accept OIDC flows that lack org claims by prompting the user to confirm company name after SSO before completing claim.
3) Longer-term: Increase claim token TTL to 30 minutes and add stronger client clock skew tolerance.

I'll open a Coupa support ticket to confirm there's no downstream issue on their side and provide the log traces (link: https://coupa.example/ticket/INC-789412).

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Hi Marta — quick update and workaround below. Apologies again for the trouble.

What happened (short): our claim flow expects an organization attribute after SSO; when Google returns only an email we couldn't bind the claim to your session and the UI showed an expiry message even though you completed the login. There is also a small client clock-skew sensitivity that can flip the UI to expired in edge cases.

Workaround (immediate):
- I've manually created a supplier record for SolValve in Coupa using the W-9 you provided.
- You should receive a direct Coupa invite (different link) from Coupa that will let you set the login method for the supplier account — please use that link rather than the original claim flow.
- If you prefer to keep using Google SSO for sign-in, please confirm the exact Google email (e.g., marta.lopez@gmail.com or marta@solvalve.es) so we can map it.

Attached: manual_invite_instructions.pdf — steps to accept the direct Coupa invite and set up a password if you want a non-SSO fallback.

If you run into any issue while accepting the invite, reply to this thread and we'll walk through it in real time (I can also start a quick Zoom if needed).

Thanks for your patience — we understand PO timing matters and we should have you set up by EOD.

Best,
